title: My Rights, Body Safety & Safe Secrets (Child Track)
description: Child-friendly lesson teaching that every child has the right to feel safe, own their body boundaries, say no to unwanted touch, and tell a trusted adult about unsafe secrets.

content.title: Foundations & Baseline Understanding: My Rights, Body Safety & Safe Secrets (Child Track)
content.overview: This section provides a trauma-informed, practical guide to understanding the core purpose of my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) and how it shapes physical, emotional, and relational safety in daily family life. Designed for children learning age-appropriate personal safety, boundaries, and rights (SS-CHD-009), it focuses on realistic, repeatable steps that strengthen safety, predictability, and connection.
content.psychoeducation: Why does my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) matter in section 1? Children and families thrive on predictability, nervous-system safety, and attuned repair. When my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) is practised consistently, stress responses decrease and relational trust grows. By focusing on understanding the core purpose of my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) and how it shapes physical, emotional, and relational safety in daily family life, caregivers and practitioners create a calmer, safer environment where children can regulate and develop confidence.
learning_goals: Define what my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) means in your own words before and after learning.
Recognise how my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) supports child safety, emotional wellbeing, and nervous-system regulation.
Practise simple, non-defensive scripts and responses for my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) during everyday moments.
Identify early warning signs, barriers, and support pathways related to my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
step_by_step: Pause & Ground: Notice your own breathing, body tension, and tone before addressing my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
Observe Factually: Notice what is happening in the moment around my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) without blame or judgement.
Connect & Validate: Acknowledge feelings and safety needs clearly and calmly.
Respond Simply: Choose one clear, age-appropriate action or boundary for my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
Reflect & Repair: Review what worked, repair any rupture honestly, and record your next small step.
parent_scripts: "I can see this moment feels big right now. Let's slow down and take one step together with my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track)."
"Everyone is safe here. We can talk about what happened and work out the next step calmly."
"I noticed I was getting stressed. I'm taking a breath so I can listen properly."
"We don't have to get everything perfect today — we are practising my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) one routine at a time."
practical_examples: Everyday Routine: Applying my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) during a busy morning or bedtime transition by slowing down, offering two calm choices, and keeping tone steady.
Moment of Stress: When tension rises around my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track), pausing for 10 seconds before speaking, validating feelings, and focusing on safety first.
Follow-Through & Review: Recording a factual note after practising my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) to notice what helped the child settle and what support would help next time.

When is my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) easiest to practise, and what triggers make it hardest?

Choose one daily routine this week to practise a calm, 2-sentence script for my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
Identify one trusted person, support service, or caseworker check-in to share your progress on my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
Write a brief, factual reflection note describing one moment you practised my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) and how your child responded.
content.closing_message: Progress in my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) comes from small, consistent moments of safety, honesty, and repair — not perfection. Every time you pause, stay regulated, and choose a safer response, you build lasting trust.

content_variants.toddlers: For babies & toddlers (0–4): Focus on gentle tone, physical comfort, predictable routines, and simple 3-to-5 word reassurance while practising my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
content_variants.school_age: For school-age children (5–11): Use clear explanations, visual routines, curiosity about their feelings, and collaborative problem-solving around my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
content_variants.teens: For adolescents (12–18): Respect autonomy, listen without lecturing, agree on clear safety boundaries, and involve teens in decisions about my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
content_variants.fatherhood: For fathers & male caregivers: Model calm accountability, steady emotional presence, and non-frightening leadership when practising my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).

red_flags: Immediate physical danger, threats, intimidation, or coercive control observed during my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
A child shows fear, freezing, dissociation, or disclosure of harm related to my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
An adult is unable to regulate or maintain safe supervision while attempting my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track).
Signs of acute mental health crisis or substance intoxication affecting child safety.
when_to_escalate: Pause learning immediately if anyone is in danger and use verified emergency or crisis supports.
Follow jurisdiction-specific child protection and mandatory reporting obligations when harm is disclosed or suspected.
Engage a qualified supervisor, specialist DFV practitioner, or clinician when risk exceeds self-directed learning.

sections.simplified_parent_version:
What my rights, body safety & safe secrets (child track) means:
My Rights, Body Safety & Safe Secrets (Child Track) is about keeping daily life safe, calm, and predictable so your child feels supported and understood.

How to practise it:
1. Pause and take one slow breath first.
2. Notice what your child needs right now.
3. Use a calm voice and one clear step.
4. Repair kindly if things go off track.
